text: Hi, my name is Jean Lemberg I live at 528 Grove Street. Up until now, elected officials at every level of government have failed to adequately address the impact of climate change. So it is up to you to consider the climate change crisis with every decision that you make. There are three strategies that will help you with this task. The first is the precautionary principle, which states when an activity raises threats of harm to human health, or the environment precautionary measures should be taken, even if some cause and effect relationships are not fully established scientifically. In this context, the proponent of an activity, rather than the public should bear the burden of proof. There is a proposal as you know, to install synthetic turf athletic fields at Edison Intermediate School, and the Memorial and Elm Street fields. The plastic grass blades and backing material contain PFS, a class of chemicals which do not break down over time, have been linked to numerous health issues and environmental concerns and bio accumulate in humans and other living creatures. Instead of adding four new synthetic turf fields to the three, which already exist in Westfield, the precautionary principles suggests exploring safer alternatives, such as organically maintained modern grass athletic fields designed and installed by a sports field management expert. Proponents of synthetic turf claim that it is safe, because it has been in existence for 50 years, has been in use at Kalar field for over 15 years, and is prevalent in surrounding communities. But those claims, no matter how many times they are repeated, are irrelevant, and do not prove product safety. This is doubly true when it is known that the materials contain known carcinogens and release greenhouse gases. The second strategy is to determine whether the claimed benefits of the proposals make sense. It sounds simple, but it can be really difficult to discern fact from fiction, especially when it comes to environmental hazards and climate change. Synthetic turf is installed outside, where it is expected to withstand the elements and daily usage for 8 to 10 years. Does it make sense that new synthetic turf fields are biodegradable? Or is this claim just another form of greenwashing by the synthetic turf industry? The amount of plastic used to construct one synthetic turf field is equivalent to 3.2 million single-use plastic bags, the same type of bag that will no longer be available in New Jersey starting on May 4. With that thought in mind, does it make sense to install any new synthetic turf fields in Westfield, which has set being a premier sustainable town as a key objective for 2022? The Edison Field Project is projected to cost $9 million, but for that same amount of money, organically maintained modern grass fields could be installed at every Westfield school. Does it make sense to spend $9 million to enable a few hundred travel team athletes to practice on two synthetic turf fields? Or would that money be better spent on upgrading every Board of Education property, which would benefit all of the nearly 6,000 students who currently attend Westfield schools? The third and final strategy is to consider whether your decisions create collateral damage. Replacing nearly six acres of natural grass with plastic carpet and ground-up tires will deny current and future EIS students the well-documented cognitive and mental health benefits provided by spending time outdoors in natural settings. It will be nearly impossible to keep pieces of plastic grass and crumb rubber particles from migrating off the field and into the school building. Therefore, EIS students and staff will be exposed to the health hazards associated with synthetic turf throughout the school day. Finally, Lifelong Westfield, one of the mayor's advisory councils, has a goal of helping Westfield residents age in place. The plan to install synthetic turf fields with stadium-like towers in residential neighborhoods is not in keeping with this noble goal. The current plans send a clear message that youth travel team athletes are more important than the older residents who want to remain in their homes free from bright lights, loud noises, and extra traffic at night. In closing, I hope that you will remember that the decisions you make as members of the Westfield Town Council will have a ripple effect that extends far beyond Westfield, New Jersey, and this moment in time. Thank you for listening.
